claims.text: This trip was priced on an UPFRONT_QUOTE fare model: fare_breakdown.quoted_fare_sgd is 29.00 and fare_breakdown.total_charged is 51.30, with fare_breakdown.quoted_fare_sgd non-null. POL-RD-11 therefore governs. The live question is not what a detour cost the rider on distance and time — those lines were fixed at booking — but what was taken above the quote.

Under POL-RD-11(a) the rider's remedy is the amount by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09, refunded in full. The only such line on this trip is the SGD 3.00 ERP charge, and it is properly chargeable: the fare_breakdown's gantry CTE (Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 towards City) is recorded as on_optimal_route true, and the trace's nearest fix to that gantry is 0.0 m away at fix index 86, well inside the 250 m match radius. The arithmetic is therefore 51.30 minus (29.00 + 3.00) = SGD 19.30 — exactly the 'other nineteen thirty' the rider queried.

The rider does not need a deviation found, and I do not ask for one. The trace measures 14.57 km against an optimal 14.2 km — an excess of 0.37 km and 2.6%, below both POL-RD-01 gates of 0.8 km and 20% — so no deviation is established. That does not touch this claim: POL-RD-11(a) is a standalone entitlement on any upfront-quoted trip and is written without any deviation condition, and it sits in the same family as the billing-integrity relief POL-RD-01 expressly preserves as available 'whether or not a deviation exists'. A metered fare charged in place of a binding quote is a billing defect, not a routing finding.

The 22.30 charged over the quote cannot be explained by anything the vehicle actually did. The trace excess is 0.37 km and the trip ran 26.0 minutes against an optimal 21.0 — five minutes more. At the rate card carried in the policy's fare_model (0.75 per km, 0.28 per minute) the whole overrun is worth about 0.28 + 1.40 = SGD 1.68, not SGD 22.30. The remaining money is a metered charge the rider never agreed to, and POL-RD-11 does not make it payable.

The ledger records fare_breakdown.payment_status as CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd as 0.00, so whatever the rider was told in app support, the record before this tribunal shows the 51.30 still collected and nothing returned. Under POL-GEN-03 the outcome NO_ACTION would leave exactly that state standing against this rider, because NO_ACTION is party-relative and on a rider-filed dispute it leaves the charge in place. For the 19.30 to move, the ruling has to move it.

No offsetting entitlement to the driver exists. POL-RD-04's compensation limb requires the rider to have been billed for LESS distance than the gps_trace records, by more than 1.0 km. Here the billed distance is 14.6 km against a trace of 14.57 km — the rider was billed at or slightly above what was driven, so the shortfall is nil and no compensation is engaged. Nothing reduces the 19.30 payable to the rider.

The driver is the only other party and he does not contest the arithmetic: his statement is that 'the app added something at the end, I don't know what'. He names no instruction from the rider, and none could be shown — the trip's chat export carries 0 messages, so the rider-instruction route in POL-RD-04 cannot be run at all. Nor is there any traffic advisory in the pool: EV-ADVIS-00533-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so the closure route in POL-RD-03 has nothing to stand on either. I disclose that artifact's 0.0 weight and its issue code expressly; its absence is itself citable and no exoneration can be built on it.

No corroboration burden beyond the trace falls on this rider. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 enhanced-corroboration trigger — 4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated — does not fire, and this rider's account of the bill is not to be discounted for claim frequency.

claims.text: This trip's own GPS trace shows no route deviation at all. Measured on the figure POL-RD-01 makes governing — the trace, trace_distance_km 14.57 km, against the booked optimal 14.2 km — the excess is 0.37 km, which is 2.6% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH tests to pass: the excess must exceed 0.8 km in absolute terms AND exceed 20% of optimal. The excess fails the absolute test by more than half a kilometre and the percentage test by a factor of roughly eight. The trip_record's rounded 14.6 km copy is expressly not citable for this test, and in any event it moves the figure by 0.03 km and changes nothing.

Because both POL-RD-01 establishment tests fail, no deviation exists and POL-RD-01 fixes the outcome as NO_ACTION 'however the rider characterises the trip'. The only carve-out that clause allows on a no-deviation trip is a billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4), and for the reasons below no such failure exists here. The rider's complaint is a re-characterisation of an ordinary, on-route trip, and POL-RD-01 anticipates exactly that.

The fare model on this trip is UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd of SGD 29.00, so the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and a detour costs the rider nothing on those lines. Under POL-RD-11, POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess — and on this trace there is no excess to speak of. The distance/time machinery on which the rider's 'nineteen thirty' theory depends simply does not apply to an upfront-quoted trip.

The single ERP line of SGD 3.00 is genuine and properly chargeable. The trace passes the CTE (Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 towards City) gantry at a nearest-fix distance of 0.0 m at fix index 86, timestamped 09:41:00, and the gantry is recorded as lying on the optimal route. It is a matched, on-optimal-route pass-through, so no POL-RD-09 correction is owed on it. Equally, the airport surcharge line is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport — there is no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge, so the POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity step does not fire.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show, citing evidence, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace. The trace here is unimpaired on its face — 100% coverage, 157 fixes at the expected 10 s cadence, zero gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 — and it yields 0.37 km / 2.6%, below threshold. The rider's burden is therefore not discharged, and the driver is not required to point to any exculpatory artifact or clause to defeat a claim that was never made out.

No MATERIAL deviation exists on this trip, so POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is not engaged and no conduct referral can arise from it. Even if the check were run, the driver's trailing-90-day deviation figure is zero flags across 250 completed trips — the opposite of the repeated long-haul pattern that clause exists to catch. The record gives the tribunal no basis for any POL-RD-06 uplift.

Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION is party-relative and leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status and fare_breakdown.refund_issued_sgd exactly as they stand. On this record the payment status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00 — no refund has issued. A NO_ACTION outcome therefore leaves the charged fare in place and returns nothing to the rider; it does not, and cannot, be read as restoring or increasing any charge.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the fare on this trip was over-collected, and SGD 19.30 goes back to the rider. Here is how that figure is reached.

First, there was no route deviation. Measured on the figure POL-RD-01 makes governing — the GPS trace, trace_distance_km 14.57 km — against the booked optimal of 14.2 km, the excess is 0.37 km, or 2.6% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed both 0.8 km and 20%; it fails both, by a wide margin (the trip_record's 14.6 km is a rounded copy and is not citable for this test). So the driver is not at fault for the route, and no distance-or-time refund arises on that account.

The money, however, is a different matter, and this is where the driver's advocate's central claim — that the failed deviation test fixes the outcome as NO_ACTION — does not survive. This was an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and the fare was fixed at booking at quoted_fare_sgd SGD 29.00. POL-RD-11 governs such trips, and POL-RD-11(a) gives the rider a standalone entitlement with no deviation condition attached: the amount by which the charged total exceeds the quote plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09 is refunded in full. The charged total is SGD 51.30. The only properly chargeable pass-through is the SGD 3.00 ERP at the CTE (Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 towards City) gantry, which the trace passes at a nearest-fix distance of 0.0 m (fix index 86, 09:41:00) and which is recorded as lying on the optimal route; there is no airport surcharge and no waiting-time fee. The refund is therefore 51.30 − (29.00 + 3.00) = SGD 19.30 — precisely the 'other nineteen thirty' the rider queried. This is a PARTIAL_REFUND: the rider still owes the quoted fare plus the ERP that was genuinely crossed, and gets back the rest.

The rider's advocate is right that the excess over the quote is not explained by anything the vehicle did, but the refund is not limited to the ~SGD 1.68 the rate card would attribute to the small overrun; under POL-RD-11(a) the whole amount taken above the quote plus pass-throughs is returned. That claim is accepted, and the figure it yields is 19.30, not 1.68.

The driver's companion claims are also addressed. The ERP line (SGD 3.00) is genuine and matched, so no POL-RD-09 correction is owed on it, and no phantom gantry or wrongly applied surcharge exists — the airport surcharge line is 0.00 — so no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral arises. No driver compensation is payable: POL-RD-04's compensation limb requires the rider to have been billed for more than 1.0 km less than the trace records, and here the billed 14.6 km equals the 14.57 km driven, so the shortfall is nil. POL-RD-06 is not engaged because there is no MATERIAL deviation, and in any event the driver's trailing-90-day deviation figure (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d) is zero. The rider's claim that no enhanced corroboration burden applies is accepted: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so the POL-RD-08 trigger does not fire.

The missing traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00533-01, is disclosed for completeness: it is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. Its absence is citable but it carries no fact and no exoneration for either side, and no part of this ruling rests on it. No exculpatory clause is invoked against it. Every artifact that does carry a deciding figure in this ruling — EV-FARE-00533 and EV-GPS-00533 — is at weight_multiplier 1.0, so confidence is not discounted, and no escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires (the trace is unimpaired, the trip identifiers all match, and no unexplained charge line lacks a counterpart in the trace or trip record).

To both parties: this case is decided on the fare ledger, and the arithmetic is not in dispute.

Route. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00533) measures 14.57 km driven against a booked optimal of 14.2 km — an excess of 0.37 km, or 2.6%. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only if the excess exceeds BOTH 0.8 km and 20% of optimal; it fails both by a wide margin. The trace is clean (100% coverage, 157 fixes at the expected 10 s cadence, max gap 0.0 s), so there is no impairment under POL-RD-07 and no gap-handling or corroboration rule applies. I therefore find no route deviation, which both advocates accept, and the driver's 'I drove the normal route' is consistent with the trace.

Money. The fare was priced UPFRONT_QUOTE (EV-FARE-00533, fare_breakdown.fare_model), quoted_fare_sgd 29.00, total_charged 51.30. On an upfront quote POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund arises — the driver is right about that — but POL-RD-11 governs instead. POL-RD-11(a) entitles the rider to any amount by which the charge exceeds the quote plus the pass-through lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. The only such line is the SGD 3.00 ERP at the CTE (Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 towards City) gantry: it is recorded on_optimal_route true and the trace passes it at a nearest-fix distance of 0.0 m at fix index 86, so it is properly chargeable and is not refunded. Waiting time fee is 0.00 and no airport surcharge applies. The correct charge was therefore 29.00 + 3.00 = 32.00, and the excess taken is 51.30 − 32.00 = SGD 19.30 — exactly the 'other nineteen thirty' the rider queried. That sum is refunded in full (it already sits on a 0.05 step).

Claims addressed. The driver's claim that POL-RD-01 fixes the outcome at NO_ACTION is rejected: POL-RD-01 closes the deviation route, but it expressly preserves billing relief, and POL-RD-11(a) is a standalone entitlement written without any deviation condition. The ledger still records payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so nothing has been returned on the record and the charge stands unless this ruling moves it. The driver's claim that the ERP line is genuine and that there is no billing-integrity failure is accepted: there is no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge. The rider's 19.30 figure is accepted. The rider's point that no POL-RD-04 compensation arises is also accepted — billed distance 14.6 km is at, not below, the 14.57 km trace, so no unbilled-distance shortfall exists and no driver compensation is engaged.

Referrals. None. POL-RD-06(c) requires a MATERIAL deviation, and none exists here; POL-RD-09(4) requires an unmatched charge line or a wrongly applied surcharge, and neither exists.

Evidence weight. The deciding facts (quoted fare, charged total, ERP line) are carried by the fare breakdown at weight_multiplier 1.0, so no impairment caps confidence and no POL-RD-10(1) escalation arises. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00533-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT); the rider disclosed it correctly, it carries no deciding fact, and no exoneration was built on it, so it neither caps confidence nor triggers escalation. The driver's statement that 'the app added something at the end' supports the refund but carries no weight_multiplier and so does not enter the cap. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires.

To the rider: you are owed SGD 19.30. To the driver: no deviation is found against you, and no compensation is due to you either. Here is why.

This was an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip (fare_breakdown.fare_model = UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd = 29.00). You were quoted SGD 29.00 and the ledger shows total_charged of SGD 51.30, with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 — so whatever in-app support told you, the record before this tribunal still shows the 51.30 collected and nothing returned. POL-RD-11 governs an upfront-quoted trip: the distance and time charges are fixed at booking, so POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available. But POL-RD-11(a) gives you a standalone entitlement to the amount by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. The only such line here is the ERP of SGD 3.00, and it is properly chargeable: the CTE (Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 towards City) gantry lies on the optimal route and the trace's nearest fix is 0.0 m from it, well inside the 250 m match radius. Waiting time fee is 0.00 and there is no airport surcharge. The arithmetic is therefore 51.30 − (29.00 + 3.00) = SGD 19.30. That is the 'other nineteen thirty' you queried, and it is refunded in full. The remaining 32.00 (your 29.00 quote plus the 3.00 ERP you did cross) stands.

On the route: there is no deviation, and both sides agree on this. On the figure POL-RD-01 makes governing — the trace, trace_distance_km 14.57 km, against the booked optimal 14.2 km — the excess is 0.37 km, or 2.6%, failing both gates (0.8 km absolute and 20%). The trip_record's rounded 14.6 km copy is expressly not citable for this test. Because no MATERIAL deviation exists, POL-RD-06 is not engaged (and in any case driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across 250 completed trips), so no driver-conduct referral arises. But the driver's argument that a no-deviation trip must end in NO_ACTION is rejected: POL-RD-01's 'no deviation, no action' rule governs the deviation remedy and expressly preserves billing relief available whether or not a deviation exists, and POL-RD-11(a) is the same kind of standalone entitlement. A binding quote was in place; billing 51.30 against it is precisely the billing defect POL-RD-11(a) answers, and no routing finding is needed to reach it.

No POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral fires: the single ERP line is matched to the trace and on the optimal route, and there is no phantom gantry and no mis-applied airport surcharge. The driver's statement — 'the app added something at the end, I don't know what' — is an admission that the extra charge was not for the route and is consistent with this finding, though it carries no weight multiplier and does not move the cap.

Evidentiary notes. EV-ADVIS-00533-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT); no exoneration is built on it. The chat log is empty (0 messages), so no rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04 can be run, and no closure under POL-RD-03 is asserted. The driver is owed no compensation: billed distance 14.6 km against 14.57 km driven leaves no shortfall exceeding 1.0 km. The rider's claim-frequency corroboration trigger under POL-RD-08 does not fire (deviation_claims_60d = 0).

The deciding facts — the quoted fare, the charged total, and the matched on-route ERP — are carried by EV-FARE-00533 and EV-GPS-00533, both at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0.

Both of you: this is an upfront-quoted trip, and the money question is answered by POL-RD-11, not by a routing finding. The booking quote was SGD 29.00 and the card was charged SGD 51.30 (EV-FARE-00533: fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 29.00, total_charged 51.30, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). POL-RD-11 fixes the distance and time charges at booking, so POL-RD-02's fare recomputation does not run. The rider's remedy is the amount by which the total charged exceeds the quote plus the pass-through lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. The only such line is the SGD 3.00 ERP charge for the CTE (Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 towards City) gantry, and it is properly chargeable: the gantry lies on the optimal route and the trace passes within 0.0 m of it at fix 86, well inside the 250 m match radius (EV-GPS-00533). No airport surcharge applies (the trip neither begins nor ends at an airport) and waiting_time_fee is 0.00. Payable = 29.00 + 3.00 = SGD 32.00. Charged = SGD 51.30. Refund = 51.30 - 32.00 = SGD 19.30, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 (already exact). That is the 'other nineteen thirty' the rider queried. RIDER'S CLAIMS. The rider is right that no deviation needs to be found for this remedy to run, and that the overrun at the rate card (roughly SGD 1.68) does not account for the 22.30 taken over the quote; POL-RD-11(a) refunds the excess over the quote plus properly chargeable pass-throughs in full whether or not it is explained. The rider is also right that the record shows 51.30 still charged and nothing refunded, so the refund must be ordered. No offsetting driver entitlement arises: billed distance 14.6 km against a trace of 14.57 km leaves no shortfall over the 1.0 km POL-RD-04 threshold, so the driver's compensation limb is not engaged. DRIVER'S CLAIMS. The driver is correct that the trace shows no deviation — 14.57 km against an optimal 14.2 km is 0.37 km / 2.6%, below both POL-RD-01 gates — and I so find. But that does not dispose of the case: POL-RD-11(a) is triggered by the fare model and the overcharge, not by a routing finding, so the absence of a deviation does not defeat the refund. The driver's submission that POL-RD-01 fixes NO_ACTION is rejected: POL-RD-01's no-deviation outcome governs the deviation finding, while the money on an upfront-quoted trip is governed by POL-RD-11, which refunds the overcharge in full. I accept the driver's points that the ERP line is genuine and matched (no POL-RD-09 pass-through correction is owed) and that no POL-RD-06 check is engaged — there is no material deviation and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across 250 trips. The driver's own statement, that the app added something at the end, is consistent with an overcharge; it carries no weight multiplier and is not needed, because the finding rests on the ledger. No exoneration applies: the chat export holds 0 messages (EV-CHAT-00533), so no rider-requested detour can be run under POL-RD-04, and EV-ADVIS-00533-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so no closure can be run under POL-RD-03. CONFIDENCE. The deciding facts — the quote, the total charged and the ERP line — are carried by EV-FARE-00533 and EV-GPS-00533, both at weight 1.0, so the cap is 1.0; I set confidence at 0.92. No escalation trigger fires, and there are no referrals: the ERP line is matched, so POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity does not fire, and the absence of a material deviation means POL-RD-06(c) conduct review does not fire.

Nothing reduces the 19.30 payable to the rider.

The driver is the only other party and he does not contest the arithmetic: his statement is that 'the app added something at the end, I don't know what'. He names no instruction from the rider, and none could be shown — the trip's chat export carries 0 messages, so the rider-instruction route in POL-RD-04 cannot be run at all. Nor is there any traffic advisory in the pool: EV-ADVIS-00533-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so the closure route in POL-RD-03 has nothing to stand on either. I disclose that artifact's 0.0 weight and its issue code expressly; its absence is itself citable and no exoneration can be built on it.

No corroboration burden beyond the trace falls on this rider. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 enhanced-corroboration trigger — 4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated — does not fire, and this rider's account of the bill is not to be discounted for claim frequency.

This trip's own GPS trace shows no route deviation at all. Measured on the figure POL-RD-01 makes governing — the trace, trace_distance_km 14.57 km, against the booked optimal 14.2 km — the excess is 0.37 km, which is 2.6% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH tests to pass: the excess must exceed 0.8 km in absolute terms AND exceed 20% of optimal. The excess fails the absolute test by more than half a kilometre and the percentage test by a factor of roughly eight. The trip_record's rounded 14.6 km copy is expressly not citable for this test, and in any event it moves the figure by 0.03 km and changes nothing.

Because both POL-RD-01 establishment tests fail, no deviation exists and POL-RD-01 fixes the outcome as NO_ACTION 'however the rider characterises the trip'. The only carve-out that clause allows on a no-deviation trip is a billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4), and for the reasons below no such failure exists here. The rider's complaint is a re-characterisation of an ordinary, on-route trip, and POL-RD-01 anticipates exactly that.

The fare model on this trip is UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd of SGD 29.00, so the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and a detour costs the rider nothing on those lines. Under POL-RD-11, POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess — and on this trace there is no excess to speak of. The distance/time machinery on which the rider's 'nineteen thirty' theory depends simply does not apply to an upfront-quoted trip.

The single ERP line of SGD 3.00 is genuine and properly chargeable. The trace passes the CTE (Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 towards City) gantry at a nearest-fix distance of 0.0 m at fix index 86, timestamped 09:41:00, and the gantry is recorded as lying on the optimal route. It is a matched, on-optimal-route pass-through, so no POL-RD-09 correction is owed on it. Equally, the airport surcharge line is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport — there is no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge, so the POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity step does not fire.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show, citing evidence, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace. The trace here is unimpaired on its face — 100% coverage, 157 fixes at the expected 10 s cadence, zero gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 — and it yields 0.37 km / 2.6%, below threshold. The rider's burden is therefore not discharged, and the driver is not required to point to any exculpatory artifact or clause to defeat a claim that was never made out.

No MATERIAL deviation exists on this trip, so POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is not engaged and no conduct referral can arise from it. Even if the check were run, the driver's trailing-90-day deviation figure is zero flags across 250 completed trips — the opposite of the repeated long-haul pattern that clause exists to catch. The record gives the tribunal no basis for any POL-RD-06 uplift.

Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION is party-relative and leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status and fare_breakdown.refund_issued_sgd exactly as they stand. On this record the payment status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00 — no refund has issued. A NO_ACTION outcome therefore leaves the charged fare in place and returns nothing to the rider; it does not, and cannot, be read as restoring or increasing any charge.
